rationale: The assistant reached the correct cause (clock not set after a power cut) in the second turn, gave accurate Neff-specific clock-setting steps, and the customer confirmed the oven heated, matching the hidden truth with no part or engineer needed. The main weakness is the opening message: a long, US-centric generic dump (breaker panel, 240V double breaker, broiler, Sabbath mode, gas igniter 'fairly cheap part') delivered before any questions, which is poorly suited to a UK homeowner and speculates about failed parts prematurely, though it did include the clock-not-set possibility and stopped short of recommending any purchase. Follow-up questions were well chosen and the close-out advice was practical.
